title: Prescription Insurance on File — Prior Authorization Decision Clocks, Emergency Supply and Approval Terms by Plan Class
content:
For each plan class of **Prescription Insurance on File**, the plan sets the clock on which it must decide a prior authorization request, the emergency supply it pays while a request waits, how long an approval lasts when the plan names no other end date, how early a renewal may be started, and the channel through which Kestrel submits the request.

## Terms

- **Standard decision hours** — hours from prior authorization submission to the plan's standard decision deadline.
- **Expedited decision hours** — hours from submission to the decision deadline of an expedited prior authorization.
- **Emergency supply days** — days supply the plan pays for while a prior authorization is pending; 0 means none.
- **Default approval months** — calendar months an approved prior authorization lasts unless the plan states otherwise.
- **Renewal lead days** — calendar days before an approval ends from which a renewal prior authorization may be started.
- **Submission channel** — how Kestrel submits a prior authorization for the class: electronic prior authorization, or adjuster review.

## Schedule

| Plan class | Standard decision (hours) | Expedited decision (hours) | Emergency supply (days) | Default approval (months) | Renewal lead (days) | Submission channel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | 24 | 24 | 3 | 6 | 30 | Electronic prior authorization |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | 72 | 24 | 0 | 12 | 30 | Electronic prior authorization |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | 72 | 24 | 0 | 12 | 30 | Electronic prior authorization |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | 72 | 24 | 0 | 12 | 30 | Electronic prior authorization |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | 72 | 24 | 0 | 12 | 30 | Electronic prior authorization |
| Commercial Copay Plan | 72 | 24 | 0 | 12 | 30 | Electronic prior authorization |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | 120 | 72 | 0 | 6 | 14 | Adjuster review |

## Notes on the schedule

- Only the Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit pays an emergency supply while a request waits (3 days); every other class shows 0, meaning none.
- The Medicaid class decides standard and expedited requests on the same 24-hour clock.
- The Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit is the only class whose requests go to adjuster review rather than electronic prior authorization, and the only class with a 120-hour standard clock, a 72-hour expedited clock and a 14-day renewal lead.
- Approvals default to 6 months under the Medicaid and workers' compensation classes and to 12 months under the Medicare and commercial classes.
